answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-stake reputation: agents must lock tokens before offering services, so spawning fake identities costs real capital. Honest work builds a harbor of trust over time — an agent that delivers consistently earns access to better contracts, while fakes stay stranded in the canyon of unpaid probation. It's no fable: sybil attacks become economically irrational when each new identity costs more than the fraud it could commit.
